c.tagline: White-sand beaches and cool dunes on Rio's Região dos Lagos.

taxi.fareNote: City taxis are metered; ride-hailing apps like Uber and 99 are usually cheaper than street taxis, especially in summer high season.

emergency.note: 190 reaches the military police, 192 summons a SAMU ambulance, and 193 reaches the fire brigade.

hood_landmark.Braga: Rua dos Biquínis Braga Cabo Frio
hood_landmark.Peró: Praia do Peró dunes Cabo Frio
hood_landmark.Praia do Forte: Praia do Forte Cabo Frio beach

avoid.reason: Keep clear of the hillside favela areas such as Jacare away from the beachfront, particularly at night.
Phone snatching and theft of unattended beach belongings happen along Praia do Forte; keep valuables minimal after sunset.

hood_desc: The historic heart of Cabo Frio around the Boulevard Canal and Nossa Senhora da Assunção church, near the 17th-century São Mateus Fort and the São Bento canal; best for first-timers wanting shops, restaurants and services within walking distance.
The city's main beach, a long stretch of famously cool white sand backed by hotels, kiosks and restaurants; the liveliest and most convenient base for beachgoers.
A canal-side neighbourhood along the Itajuru channel lined with seafood restaurants, bars and boat moorings; good for waterfront dining and nightlife a short hop from the beaches.
A busy commercial district known for the Rua dos Biquínis (Bikini Street) beachwear market and shopping, close to Praia do Forte; suits travellers who want retail and easy beach access.
A quieter residential beach area to the north with the long Praia do Peró and protected sand dunes; suits families and travellers wanting calmer sands and nature.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water, as visitors do throughout Brazil.

transit.hours: Municipal buses run roughly 05:00 to around midnight, thinning out late at night; taxis and ride apps fill the gap.
transit.note: Cabo Frio has no metro or tram; getting around relies on municipal buses, taxis and ride-hailing apps, plus a very walkable beachfront and canal district.
transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash to the driver (or with the regional RioCard where accepted); there is no citywide smartcard.

bus: Intercity coaches to Rio de Janeiro, Búzios and the Região dos Lagos (Auto Viação 1001, Salineira, Montes Brancos)

tip.r: A 10% service charge is usually already added to restaurant bills; extra tipping is optional.
